edits.hebrew: מתני׳ הורו ב"ד וידע אחד מהן שטעו ואמר להן טועין אתם או שלא היה מופלא של ב"ד שם או שהיה אחד מהן גר או ממזר או נתין או זקן שלא ראוי לבנים ה"ז פטור שנאמ' כאן עדה ונאמר להלן עדה מה עדה האמורה להלן כולן ראוין להוראה אף עדה האמורה כאן עד שיהיו כולן ראוין להוראה:
edits.english: MISHNA: If the court issued a ruling, and one of the judges knew that they erred and he said to them: You are mistaken; or if the most distinguished [mufla] member of the court was not there for that session of the Sanhedrin, or if one of the judges was disqualified from serving as a judge, e.g., because he was a convert, or a child born from an incestuous or adulterous relationship [mamzer], or a Gibeonite, or an old man no longer able to father children, this court is exempt, because they have not rendered a full-fledged ruling. This is derived by means of a verbal analogy, as “assembly” is stated here with regard to a court that issues an erroneous ruling: “And if the entire assembly of Israel shall act unwittingly” (Leviticus 4:13), and “assembly” is stated there with regard to the halakha of one who commits murder unwittingly: “And the assembly shall judge between the one who struck and the blood redeemer” (Numbers 35:24). Just as in the “assembly” stated there, with regard to the unwitting murderer, all the judges must be fit to issue rulings, so too, in the “assembly” stated here, with regard to the court that issued an erroneous ruling; the court will not be liable unless all the judges will be fit to issue rulings.

edits.hebrew: ואמר להם טועים אתם - לא הוי הוראה מעליא ופטור, דבעינן עד שיורו כולן כדאמר לעיל:
edits.english: And he said to them: You are mistaken - This is not considered a proper ruling, and they are exempt, because we require that all of them issue the ruling, as stated above.

edits.hebrew: או שלא היה מופלא של ב"ד שם - אף על גב דלא הוה מסנהדרין עצמן, דאילו הוי מסנהדרין עצמן, אפילו (אם) קטן שבכולן לא היה שם, לא הויא הוראה מעליא, כדאמר לקמן מאם כל עדת איתא לכולה סנהדרי הויא הוראה ואי לא לא. ואיכא למימר: נצטרך אחד מהן לצאת לדרך ומינו אחר במקומו, או נמי זקן (או) שאין לו בנים היה, לכך נתמנה אחר בסנהדרין:
edits.english: Or if the most distinguished member of the court was not there - Even though he was not from the Sanhedrin members themselves, for if he was from the Sanhedrin members themselves, even if the youngest among them was not there, it would not be a proper ruling, as it says later from 'if the entire assembly' that the entire Sanhedrin must be present for it to be a ruling, and if not, then not. And one might say: One of them needed to go on a journey and they appointed another in his place; or alternatively, he was an old man who had no children, and therefore another was appointed to the Sanhedrin.

edits.hebrew: או זקן שאין ראוי לבנים - וקשיא לי: מפני מה אין ראוי להוראה:
edits.english: Or an old man no longer able to father children - And it is difficult for me: Why is he not fit to issue rulings?

The court issued a ruling, and one of them knew that they erred, and he said to them: "You are mistaken"; or if the most distinguished member of the court (the greatest of the Sages) was not there in the session of the Sanhedrin that decided this, or if one of them was disqualified from the Sanhedrin, such as being a convert, or a mamzer, or a natin, or an old man no longer able to father children, as all of these are not fit to serve in the Sanhedrin — this court is exempt, for this is not a complete ruling,

The most distinguished member of the court is the greatest of the Sages, the head of the *yeshiva*, to whom all others are like students. Generally, he is the one appointed to be the *Nasi* (president) of the Sanhedrin (Rambam).

Rashi explains (in a second explanation) that there was a complete quorum of the Sanhedrin present (for all opinions agree that if the entire Sanhedrin did not issue the ruling, it is not a valid ruling), but it happened that the most distinguished member of the court went elsewhere, and another was appointed in his place temporarily to complete the quorum (and similarly in R. Chananel, and see also in Be'er Sheva and others). However, Rashi also explains another interpretation, that the most distinguished member of the court was not counted among the members of the Sanhedrin. This is possible due to various reasons, such as this great Sage having a disqualification that prevented him from being a member of the court (e.g., he had a physical blemish, or a lineage disqualification, or he was extremely old, and so on). Yet, despite these, he is the greatest of the Sages, and everyone must learn from him. Similarly, the Ri'd wrote, bringing a kind of proof from what is mentioned, 'seventy and two elders,' implying that there was an additional Sage who was not counted among the seventy-one members of the Sanhedrin (and see in the book Margaliyot HaYam, which elaborates on this view).

edits.hebrew:
ובירושלמי מסבירים שאף שאין ממנים אותם לכתחילה, מדובר כאשר עברו ומינוהו. ובפירוש אחר אמרו שלא היה ממנים הסנהדרין אבל היה עימם בזמן הדיונים.

ולעצם הענין יש שכתבו כי במקרים מיוחדים היו ממנים גם פסולים מסוג זה לסנהרין (והביאו ראיה משמעיה ואבטליון שהיו, כנראה, גרים).
edits.english:
And in the Yerushalmi, they explain that even though they are not appointed *ab initio*, it refers to a case where they transgressed and appointed him. In another explanation, they said that he was not appointed to the Sanhedrin but was with them during the deliberations.

Regarding the matter itself, some have written that in special cases, even disqualified individuals of this type were appointed to the Sanhedrin (and they brought proof from Shemaya and Avtalyon, who were, apparently, converts).

edits.hebrew: בענין גר או ממזר יש מקום לומר את שניהם, כי גר בא מטיפה פסולה, וממזר פסול לבוא בקהל, אבל לכאורה נתין פסול מכל צד, ומה טעם נאמר? ותירצו כי איסור הנתינים (לפי כמה שיטות) אינו אלא מדברי סופרים (גזירת דוד המלך), ולכן הוצרך לומר שאף הוא פסול (חק נתן).
edits.english: Regarding a convert or a *mamzer*, there is room to mention both, because a convert comes from a flawed drop (of seed), and a *mamzer* is disqualified from entering the congregation. But seemingly, a *natin* is disqualified from all sides, so what reason is there to mention him? They answered that the prohibition of *netinim* (according to several views) is only by rabbinic decree (a decree of King David), and therefore it was necessary to state that he too is disqualified (Chok Natan).

edits.hebrew:
בהרבה מקורות גרסו: זקן ושלא ראוי לבנים, כשני מקרים שונים (וכך נראה מפסק ההלכה של הרמב"ם בענין זה).

רש"י שואל: מה טעם פסולו של זה? והעיר בספר ב"ש שבמסכת סנהדרין מסביר רש"י עצמו את טעם הדבר שמי שלא היו לו בנים אין בו מדת הרחמנות הנחוצה לחבר הסנהדרין. ובלח"מ מסביר ששאלת רש"י היתה: מפני מה זקן שהיו לו בנים נפסל, אף שעכשיו אינו ראוי. ובר"ח מסביר שמי שלא היו לו בנים נמצא שלא קיים מצות פריה ורביה.

אבל היו שקראו ככתוב לפנינו, שלכאורה אין ראוי להעמיד בסנהדרין זקנים, וגדר הזמן הוא כאשר הוא זקן כל כך ששוב אינו ראוי לבנים.
edits.english:
In many sources, the reading is: 'an old man *and* one who is not fit for children,' as two different cases (and this is how the Rambam's *halakhic* ruling on this matter appears).

Rashi asks: What is the reason for his disqualification? And the book Be'er Sheva noted that in Tractate Sanhedrin, Rashi himself explains the reason that one who has no children lacks the measure of compassion necessary for a member of the Sanhedrin. And in Lechem Mishneh, it explains that Rashi's question was: Why is an old man who *had* children disqualified, even if he is now unfit (to father children)? And R. Chananel explains that one who had no children has not fulfilled the mitzvah of 'be fruitful and multiply.'

However, there were those who read it as written before us, that seemingly it is not appropriate to appoint old men to the Sanhedrin, and the definition of 'old' is when he is so old that he is no longer fit to father children.

edits.hebrew: הורו בית דין בטעות להתיר איסור מן התורה, ולא היה שם ראש הישיבה ("מופלא שבבית דין") או שהיה אחד מהם מי שאינו ראוי להיות בסנהדרין, כגון גר או ממזר או זקן או מי שלא היו לו בנים (נראה שזו היתה גרסת הרמב"ם. לח"מ). וכיוצא בהם — אין זו הוראה, ובית דין פטורים, והעושים על פיהם חייבים להביא חטאת. כסתם משנה. (רמב"ם ספר קרבנות הלכות שגגות פי"ג ה"א).
edits.english: If the court erred in ruling to permit a Torah prohibition, and the head of the *yeshiva* ('most distinguished member of the court') was not present, or if one of them was unfit to be in the Sanhedrin, such as a convert, a *mamzer*, an old man, or one who had no children (it appears this was the Rambam's version, Lechem Mishneh), and similar cases — this is not a valid ruling, and the court is exempt, while those who acted upon their ruling are liable to bring a sin-offering. This is like the anonymous Mishnah (Rambam, *Sefer Korbanot*, *Hilkhot Shegagot* 13:1).

edits.hebrew: או שלא היה מופלא שבב"ד שם - פרש"י: ולא היה במנין, דאילו כן, אפילו קטן שבהם נמי כדאמרינן לעיל שיהיו כולן בהוראה. וקשה: דהא אתותב לעיל (נ"ל דצריכין לומר דלפני התו' לא היה כתוב לעיל הא דמסיק ואלא מאי כל עדת דקאמר רחמנא כו' עי' לקמן ברש"י דף (ה') [הוריות ז'] ע"א) ובתורת כהנים מוסיף נמי: אם אמר אחד 'איני יודע', דכמאן דליתיה דמיא:
edits.english: Or if the most distinguished member of the court was not there - Rashi explains: He was not part of the quorum, for if so, even the youngest among them also (being absent) would mean, as we said above, that all of them must be present for a ruling. And it is difficult: For it was refuted above (it seems necessary to say that before Tosafot, what is concluded above was not written, 'but what does the Merciful One mean by "the entire assembly," etc.' See below in Rashi, page (5) [Horayot 7a]) and in Torat Kohanim it also adds: If one said 'I do not know,' it is as if he is not present.

edits.hebrew: אחד מהן גר או ממזר - בירושלמי: שעברו ומנוהו. דמי שאין ראוי להוראה נעשה כאבן:
edits.english: One of them was a convert or a mamzer - In the Yerushalmi: They transgressed and appointed him. For one who is not fit to issue rulings becomes like a stone.
